content.comment_body: I have connected a [product_name] contact 230 to a 230V AC supply at terminals A1 & A2. Even without any load at the main terminals, the coil becomes quite hot (reaching approximately 65°C after two hours while powered). Could someone clarify if this temperature is typical for the [product_name] contact? Also, why is a solid core with diodes (intended for DC) used instead of a standard AC core? Best regards, [user_name] [user_name]@[company_name].com.pk
That temperature is standard for this [product_name] contact 230V.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is concerned that the coil of the [product_name] contact 230V reaches 65°C after two hours of operation without a connected load. Another response states this is typical, indicating the equipment functions as designed, but uncertainty remains about both the operating temperature and the design aspects.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates the [product_name] contact 230V will run cooler when energized without a load, seeking clarification on both the expected operating temperature and the reasoning for the core design.
feature_keywords: core design (with diodes/AC vs DC core)
